title: Louis as a boss: discipline and compassion toward Danny Barcelona
summary: Louis scolded Joe for lateness and talking during solos but asked the band quietly to help Danny Barcelona rather than firing him.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: How was Louis to get along with?

Great. I made more money with Louis and I had more fun, and it was the easiest job I ever had in my life. The only trouble...one time... The only bad thing Louis ever said to me, and it wasn't bad...I mean, to warn me... I was about a minute late getting on the stand, for some reason -- I had to go to the men's room. And when I got up there, he says, 'Look, that's one thing I won't tolerate. You men be on this stand. Listen, homeboy, we hit. We hit.'
And another time, Billy Kyle was taking a solo, and me and Trummy started talking. Boy, Louis got mad.
You never talked on a bandstand.

No, sir. He said, "When a man is taking a solo, anything you do to distract him... That's his spot, and you don't do nothin' to distract him, because you wouldn't want him to do it on your solo." He says, "I don't do it." And then he says, "You guys just be quiet, that's all." Outside of that, nothing.

And he was a real compassionate guy when it came to... I remember one time in particular, Danny Barcelona and his wife (Bennie was her name), they was having a terrible time, and Danny was drinking and stuff like that, and spending his money... It got so that it affected Danny's playing. And everybody in the band noticed it; Danny was throwing people off and he was playing horrible. So Louis got us backstage one day, and he said, "I want to ask you guys something? What's wrong with Danny?" He said, "I know you notice how bad he's playing. But I don't want to say anything to him, because maybe the guy..." He said, "I sure don't want to fire him." He says, "But if I say anything to him, he might get nervous and he'll play worse." He said, "If you guys could maybe drop a little hint or something..." "That's all I want to say," he says. "I like Danny." And consequently,
he said, 'He'll straighten himself out.' A lot of bandleaders would have got mad and...
But he said, 'I know he's having problems with his wife, and I ain't gonna say nothin'.' And he didn't. And finally, Danny just...everything was forgotten.
